Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 77, verses 1–15:

Explanation of the words:

{Wal-mursalati ʿurfan}: al-mursalat (the sent ones) are the good winds, and ʿurf are those that follow in succession.

{Fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan}: then the winds that blow violently, harmful because of their strength.

{Wan-nashirati nashran}: the winds that spread the rain and scatter it across the sky, spreading it out.

{Fal-mulqiyati dhikran}: i.e., the angels who convey the revelation to the prophets so that they may remind (people) of it.

{ʿUdhran aw nudhran}: i.e., as an excuse (ʿudhr) for some peoples, or as a warning (indhar) to others.

{Innama tuʿadduna la-waqiʿ}: i.e., what you are promised, O people, is certainly going to occur without doubt.

{Fa-idha al-nujumu ṭumisat}: i.e., their light is effaced and gone.

{Wa-idha al-sama'u furijat}: i.e., it is split open and cracked.

{Wa-idha al-jibalu suyyirat}: i.e., they are uprooted and become like scattered dust, dispersed here and there.

{Wa-idha al-rusulu uqqitat}: i.e., they are gathered for an appointed time set for them to attend.

{Li-yawmi al-fasl}: i.e., the Day on which Allah, exalted is He, will judge between the creatures.

Meaning of the verses:

The statement of Allah, exalted is He, {Wal-mursalati ʿurfan}, is the beginning of an oath in which Allah swears by several of His creations, and Allah may swear by whatever He wills. The wisdom of swearing is that souls may be calm regarding the report and reassured of the truthfulness of the one who reports it, and thereby the purpose of delivering the report to the listeners is achieved. The things sworn by here are: al-mursalat, which are the successive, good, pleasant winds; al-ʿasifat, among them, which are the violently blowing winds that may uproot trees and destroy buildings; al-nashirat nashran, which are the moderate winds that spread the clouds and scatter them, or drive them to bring rain and send down rain; and al-fariqat farqan, which are the verses of the Noble Qur'an that distinguish between truth and falsehood; and al-mulqiyat dhikran, ʿudhran aw nudhran, which are the angels who convey the revelation to whomever Allah, exalted is He, has chosen from among His servants, for excuse and warning, i.e., they excuse some people and warn others. This is the oath, the one swearing is Allah, and what is sworn to is His statement, majestic is His remembrance: that what you are promised, O people, of good or evil, is certainly going to occur without doubt. Therefore, set your deeds right after correcting your intentions, for the recompense is certain to occur and will never fail, never change, and never be altered. When will this promised certain thing occur? The answer: it occurs on the Day of Judgment (yawm al-fasl). What is the Day of Judgment? The answer: it is a day on which Allah gathers the witnesses from among the angels and the messengers and judges between people. And when does the Day of Judgment occur? The answer: when the stars are effaced, i.e., their light is gone and extinguished; when the sky is split, i.e., it is torn open and cracked; when the mountains are uprooted, i.e., they are crushed; and when the messengers are gathered, i.e., a specific time is set for them to attend, and that is the Day of Judgment. {Wa-ma adraka ma yawm al-fasl}: this is a glorification of its importance and an announcement of its terror. The statement of Allah, exalted is He, {Waylun yawma'idhin}: i.e., on the day when the judgment occurs, there is a great and terrible punishment {lil-mukadhdhibin}: for those who deny Allah, His signs, His meeting, and His messenger.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense.

2- Allah may swear by whatever He wills of His creation, but it is not for the servant to swear by other than his Creator, majestic is He.

3- Signs of the Hour and the general cosmic upheaval, namely the extinguishing of the light of the stars, the splitting of the sky, and the uprooting of the mountains.

4- A severe warning with {Waylun}, which is a valley in Hell from whose heat Hell itself seeks refuge, for those who deny what must be believed among the six pillars of faith, and the promise and threat of Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 77, verses 29–40:

Explanation of the words:

"Depart to that which you used to deny": i.e., the punishment.

"To a shadow of three branches": i.e., the smoke of Hell, when it rises, divides into three branches because of its enormity.

"Neither shady": i.e., a shelter that provides cover and protection.

"Nor does it avail against the flame": i.e., nor does it ward off any of the heat.

"Indeed, it": i.e., the Fire.

"Throws sparks like a fortress": i.e., each single spark is like a fortress in its enormity and height.

"As if it were yellow camels": i.e., the sparks flying from the Fire: each spark is like a fortress in its size and height, and like a camel in its shape and color; and the yellow camel is the black one that inclines toward yellow.

"This is a Day when they will not speak": i.e., they will not say anything in it.

"Nor will they be permitted": i.e., to make an excuse.

"We have gathered you and the former peoples": i.e., the deniers before you.

"So if you have a plan, then plot against Me": i.e., a stratagem to ward off the punishment; so devise a way to avert the punishment from yourselves.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish the doctrine of resurrection and recompense, on which all of life depends. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Depart﴾: this is said to the deniers on the Day of Resurrection while they are in its plains, said to them as rebuke and reproach: ﴿Depart to that which you used to deny﴾, which is the punishment of the Hereafter. It mocks them and scorns them, and they are told: ﴿Depart to a shadow of three branches﴾, which is the smoke of the Fire; when it rises, it divides into three branches, because of its enormity. ﴿Neither shady﴾: it is not a true shade like the shade of a tree or a wall that shelters and screens. ﴿Nor does it avail against the flame﴾, so it does not repel the heat. Exalted is He said describing it: ﴿Indeed, it﴾, i.e., the Fire, ﴿throws sparks like a fortress﴾: each single spark is like a fortress in its greatness and height. ﴿As if it were yellow camels﴾: each spark is like a yellow camel, which is the black one inclining toward yellow.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾, threatening those who deny it, His signs, His meeting, and His Messenger ﷺ. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak﴾, i.e., this is the Day of Resurrection, a Day on which they will not speak, i.e., they will not say anything in it. ﴿Nor will they be permitted﴾, i.e., to offer excuses, so they make excuses but no excuse is accepted and no permission is given for it.

Because the Day of Resurrection is long and its events are varied, the Qur'an sometimes reports their excuses and speech in one station, and denies it in another, since it is the case that in some stations they speak, even swearing falsely, while in other stations fear and grief overwhelm them so they say nothing; in some stations they are asked to speak and they speak, and in others not. ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ is a warning to all who deny this and other things. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment; We have gathered you and the former peoples﴾, i.e., it is said to them on the Day of Resurrection, while they are in its plains: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment, which you used to deny. We have gathered you in it, O deniers of this nation, and the deniers before it of the former peoples.﴾ ﴿So if you have a plan, then plot against Me﴾, i.e., a stratagem for your deliverance from what you are in; so devise against Me and free yourselves. It is said to them as rebuke and disgrace, and it is a spiritual punishment more painful than physical punishment. ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾, i.e., woe on the day when the Day of Judgment comes to the deniers.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Mockery, scorn and rebuke are among the most painful kinds of spiritual punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

2- The plains of the Resurrection are vast, the stay in them is long, and the trial in them is severe.

3- Establishing the doctrine of resurrection and recompense by mentioning some of what takes place in it.

4- Denial is the root of disbelief, and punishment follows from it.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 77, verses 41–50**

**Explanation of the Words:**

﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾: i.e., those who fear their Lord, believe in Him, and obey Him by doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes.

﴿In shade﴾: i.e., in the shade of dense trees.

﴿And springs﴾: i.e., of water, milk, wine, and honey.

﴿From whatever they desire﴾: not from what they find, as is the case in this world.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾: i.e., just as We recompense the righteous, We recompense the doers of good.

﴿Eat and enjoy﴾: i.e., in this worldly life.

﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down"﴾: i.e., pray; they do not pray.

﴿After that, in what message will they believe?﴾: i.e., after the Qur'an, since other books are not miraculous, and the Qur'an is miraculous (mu'jiz, inimitable) in its words and meanings. Whoever does not believe in the Qur'an does not believe in anything else under any circumstances.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

By way of encouragement (targhib) and warning (tarhib), a method distinctive to the Noble Qur'an, the Exalted mentions the lasting bliss prepared for the righteous after mentioning the torment of the Hellfire for the deniers who went astray. He says, ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾, who are those who avoided polytheism (shirk) and sins, ﴿are in shades and springs﴾: in the shade of the trees of Paradise and its springs, of water, milk, wine, and honey, and abundant varied fruits, ﴿from whatever they desire﴾, unlike in this world, where people eat only what they find. If they desired something and did not find it, they would not eat it. But in the abode of bliss, a person desires nothing without finding it and eating it. This is the reason for the expression "from whatever they desire" used in more than one place.

Among the completions of their bliss is that it will be said to them, to gladden their hearts: "Eat and drink with satisfaction," meaning, enjoying what you used to do of righteous deeds and abandoning of evil deeds. The Exalted's saying, ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾, means: just as We gave this reward to the righteous, We reward the doers of good with it. ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾, i.e., to those who deny this gracious promise.

His saying, ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed, you are criminals﴾: this is the statement of God, the Exalted, to the polytheists of Quraysh and their disbelievers, threatening them, the Lord, blessed and exalted, condemning their criminality until their time arrives. It had arrived, as He informed them that they would enjoy only a little, and they were destroyed at Badr. His saying, ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾, is a warning of painful punishment for whoever denies this threat of God and His promise.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down"﴾, i.e., pray, ﴿they do not bow down﴾, i.e., they do not pray, nor do they humble themselves, so that they would accept the truth and believe in it. Woe that Day to those who deny the laws and guidance of God, who abandon prayer. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Then in what message after this will they believe?﴾, i.e., in what book will these deniers believe if they do not believe in the Qur'an? This is because of the good and guidance it contains, and the happiness and perfection to which it calls, and because it is miraculous in its words and meanings, unlike other books. Whoever does not believe in it, there is no hope that he will believe in anything else under any circumstances.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense by mentioning what God, the Exalted, has prepared for His righteous, believing friends who do good.
2. Explanation of the bliss of the people of piety and beneficence, and their virtue, i.e., the virtue of piety and beneficence.
3. The truthfulness of the Qur'an in its reports, since God's threat against the greatest criminals of Mecca was carried out after less than five years.
4. Whoever enters a mosque while its people are praying should join them in their prayer, even if he has already prayed, so that he is not the only one not bowing to God. This meaning has come in the Sahih (collections of authentic hadith).

The Exalted's saying, ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾, means: just as We gave this reward to the righteous, We reward the doers of good with it. ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾, i.e., to those who deny this gracious promise.

His saying, ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed, you are criminals﴾: this is the statement of God, the Exalted, to the polytheists of Quraysh and their disbelievers, threatening them, the Lord, blessed and exalted, condemning their criminality until their time arrives. It had arrived, as He informed them that they would enjoy only a little, and they were destroyed at Badr. His saying, ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾, is a warning of painful punishment for whoever denies this threat of God and His promise.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down"﴾, i.e., pray, ﴿they do not bow down﴾, i.e., they do not pray, nor do they humble themselves, so that they would accept the truth and believe in it. Woe that Day to those who deny the laws and guidance of God, who abandon prayer. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Then in what message after this will they believe?﴾, i.e., in what book will these deniers believe if they do not believe in the Qur'an? This is because of the good and guidance it contains, and the happiness and perfection to which it calls, and because it is miraculous in its words and meanings, unlike other books. Whoever does not believe in it, there is no hope that he will believe in anything else under any circumstances.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense by mentioning what God, the Exalted, has prepared for His righteous, believing friends who do good.
2. Explanation of the bliss of the people of piety and beneficence, and their virtue, i.e., the virtue of piety and beneficence.
3. The truthfulness of the Qur'an in its reports, since God's threat against the greatest criminals of Mecca was carried out after less than five years.
4. Whoever enters a mosque while its people are praying should join them in their prayer, even if he has already prayed, so that he is not the only one not bowing to God. This meaning has come in the Sahih (collections of authentic hadith).
